changes: Every live OrderedMap entry is now an allocator-owned OrderedMapNode; every OrderedDataMap entry is an allocator-owned OrderedDataMapNode. No alternate payload struct or owning slot node remains.
BaseMapStorage owns the native bucket table; native node hash and insertion-order links are authoritative for lookup, insertion, removal, rehash, iteration and destruction.
One generic sealed engine selects the concrete native node allocation and field projections; data construction and destruction retain value-before-key and key-before-value phases.
Borrowed iterators and node views follow actual order pointers. Mutable iteration no longer allocates a snapshot Vec and projects disjoint fields without reborrowing whole nodes.

Separate non-owning identity slots, a free-slot list and pointer-address registry retain safe detached cursor owner/node validation and reused-slot behavior. No integer address is converted back into a dereferenceable pointer.

Native bucket traversal and link reversal during rehash match direct oracle rows. Actual container node payload offsets, requested typed layouts, allocator live counts, stable addresses and clear release behavior match direct native probes. Accumulating physical reservation padding is measured separately as a remaining gap.
Removal detaches every graph edge before destruction; Clear destroys bucket chains before resetting extent/order and uses shared deferred-panic cleanup to release all Rust allocations.

Send/Sync depend on payload and hasher traits; negative trait checks preserve forbidden payload/policy cases. Heap payloads remain Unpin while an inline !Unpin hasher keeps the container !Unpin; map/shared-iterator covariance remains tested.
limitations: Safe detached cursors require an extra non-owning Vec, free-slot Vec and HashMap registry; first/last identifiers and count/bucket/allocator metadata are adapted alongside BaseMapStorage. This is not a byte-for-byte native container layout or allocation-count claim for all metadata.

The existing shared accumulating typed allocator reserves align-4 bytes beyond its native raw request. For these int node probes Rust consumes 36/44 bytes versus native AccAllocator 32/40, despite matching requested node layouts. The two reservation rows explicitly document this Rust alignment safety adaptation; they are not equal-reservation parity credit.

Existing set FirstNode compatibility views expose unit as their item although actual native OrderedMapNode::Value aliases Key. Native mutable/raw node access remains a separately scoped API adaptation.
Borrowed iterator/view projection callbacks add representation overhead versus native raw typed-node iterators; detached cursor identity validation retains its prior address-reuse boundary.
Resize snapshots original bucket links for panic recovery; this extra temporary allocation restores Rust memory safety if a hash callback panics, beyond native exception guarantees.
Rust destructor panic cleanup completes pending nodes and resumes a panic; native noexcept/destructor throwing behavior is not claimed equivalent.
Existing moved-from hash-policy/bucket selection, custom C++ move callbacks, forwarding conversions and caller-visible rvalue state remain open behavior boundaries.
Concrete x86_64 scalar layout/allocation probes do not certify every generic ABI, zero-size Rust type or compiler ABI.
Observer access to native callback metadata and partially initialized raw node memory remains unproved; direct graph fixtures and callback traces do not imply arbitrary reentrant mutation support.
No global API denominator or legacy mapping credit is granted. These scoped compiler bindings/checks do not certify full OrderedMap/OrderedDataMap or whole OCCT parity.
